errors.title: Request is not valid
errors.hint: Fix each field listed in `errors` (the `pointer` names it), then send the request again.
errors.meaning: One or more request fields, path parameters or query parameters do not match the API description. The `errors` list names each field with a JSON pointer.

errors.title: Request has a field the API does not know
errors.hint: Remove or correct the field or parameter named by `errors[].pointer`; the API reference lists what each operation accepts.
errors.meaning: The request body has a field, or the query has a parameter, that the operation does not accept. Unknown fields and parameters are refused so that a misspelt one never silently does nothing.

errors.title: Bucket name is not valid
errors.hint: Choose a name of 3 to 63 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens that starts and ends with a letter or digit.
errors.meaning: Bucket names are 3 to 63 characters of lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, and start and end with a letter or digit.

errors.title: Cursor is not valid
errors.hint: Start again without `cursor`, then pass only the `next_cursor` values the API returns.
errors.meaning: The `cursor` value was not returned by this operation, was changed, or has expired.

errors.title: Authentication required
errors.hint: Send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` with an API token from the console (Account, API tokens).
errors.meaning: The request has no `Authorization` header, or the bearer token in it is not a valid Kofra API token.

errors.title: API token has expired
errors.hint: Create a new API token in the console and use it in place of the expired one.
errors.meaning: The API token was valid but has passed its expiry time.

errors.title: Token lacks a required scope
errors.hint: Use a token that has the scope named in `detail`, or create one with that scope in the console.
errors.meaning: The API token is valid but does not carry the scope this operation needs. The scopes needed are listed in the operation's description.

errors.title: Your role does not allow this
errors.hint: Ask a workspace Owner or Admin to change your role, or to perform the operation.
errors.meaning: The token has the scope, but the member it belongs to has a workspace role that does not allow the operation. Effective permission is the token's scopes limited by the member's role.

errors.title: Account is read-only
errors.hint: Resolve the reason shown under Account in the console (often a payment); writes work again as soon as the account is active.
errors.meaning: The account is suspended in read-only mode. Reads, lists and deletes work; anything that adds data or credentials is refused.

errors.title: Account is not available
errors.hint: Open Account in the console to see the reason; a deletion can be cancelled there or with POST /v1/account/deletion/cancel.
errors.meaning: The account is blocked or is being deleted, so only reading the account itself and cancelling a deletion are possible.

errors.title: No such endpoint
errors.hint: Check the path against the API reference at https://api.kofra.app/openapi.json.
errors.meaning: The path does not name an operation of this API version.

errors.title: Bucket not found
errors.hint: List your buckets with GET /v1/buckets and use one of the returned names.
errors.meaning: The workspace has no bucket with this name.

errors.title: Access key not found
errors.hint: List your access keys with GET /v1/keys and use one of the returned IDs.
errors.meaning: The workspace has no active access key with this ID. Revoked keys are removed, so a second revoke of the same key also answers this code.

errors.title: Method not allowed
errors.hint: Use one of the methods in the `Allow` header.
errors.meaning: The path exists, but not with this HTTP method. The `Allow` header lists the methods it accepts.

errors.title: Request body is too large
errors.hint: Send a smaller body; upload object data through the S3 endpoint or a presigned URL instead.
errors.meaning: Management requests carry small JSON bodies. Object data is never sent to this API; it goes to the S3 endpoint.

errors.title: Body must be JSON
errors.hint: Send the body as JSON with the header `Content-Type: application/json`.
errors.meaning: Request bodies must be sent as `application/json`.

errors.title: Bucket already exists
errors.hint: Choose another name, or use the existing bucket.
errors.meaning: The workspace already has a bucket with this name.

errors.title: Bucket is not empty
errors.hint: Delete every object in the bucket with your S3 tool, then delete the bucket again.
errors.meaning: A bucket can be deleted only when it holds no objects. Objects are deleted through the S3 endpoint.

errors.title: Too many active access keys
errors.hint: Revoke an access key you no longer use with DELETE /v1/keys/{key_id}, then create the new one.
errors.meaning: A workspace can have at most 20 active access keys at once.

errors.title: Access can only be widened
errors.hint: Create a new key with the narrower access, move your tools to it, then revoke the old key.
errors.meaning: An access key's permission on a bucket can be added or widened (from read to read_write), never narrowed. A narrowed grant could silently become wide again after a recovery, so narrowing is refused.

errors.title: Too many grants on one key
errors.hint: Create a second access key for the remaining buckets.
errors.meaning: An access key can hold grants on at most 32 buckets.

errors.title: Deletion already requested
errors.hint: Read GET /v1/account to see the deletion and its dates; cancel it with POST /v1/account/deletion/cancel if it was a mistake.
errors.meaning: The account already has a deletion in progress or awaiting confirmation.

errors.title: No deletion to cancel
errors.hint: No action is needed; the account is not being deleted.
errors.meaning: The account has no deletion in progress, so there is nothing to cancel.

errors.title: Deletion can no longer be cancelled
errors.hint: No action can restore this data; contact support with the `request_id` if you believe this is wrong.
errors.meaning: The deletion has passed its last cancellation time. Deleted data is cryptographically erased (its encryption key is destroyed), so it can never be read again.

errors.title: Event feed was reset
errors.hint: Re-read the current state (GET /v1/account, /v1/keys, /v1/usage), then read the feed again without a cursor.
errors.meaning: The event feed was rebuilt, so cursors issued before the rebuild no longer apply. Some events may not appear in the new feed.

errors.title: Same request is still running
errors.hint: Wait for the number of seconds in `Retry-After`, then send the identical request again with the same key.
errors.meaning: A request with this `Idempotency-Key` is still being processed.

errors.title: Idempotency key used with another request
errors.hint: Use a new Idempotency-Key for a different request; reuse a key only to repeat the identical request.
errors.meaning: An `Idempotency-Key` is bound to the first request sent with it for 24 hours, that is to its method, path, query and body. The same key with a different method, path, query or body is refused, so `dry_run=true` and the same request without it need different keys (`dry_run=false` and an omitted `dry_run` are the same request).

errors.title: Too many requests
errors.hint: Wait for the number of seconds in `Retry-After`, then retry; spread requests out to stay under the limit.
errors.meaning: The credential or workspace has used up its request allowance for now. The `RateLimit` and `RateLimit-Policy` headers describe the limit that applied.

errors.title: Internal error
errors.hint: Contact support and quote the `request_id`; repeating the same request is not expected to help.
errors.meaning: The request failed for a reason that is not one of the codes above. No detail of the cause is returned.

errors.title: Service is busy
errors.hint: Wait for the number of seconds in `Retry-After`, then send the same request again.
errors.meaning: The service is temporarily busy or a dependency is briefly unavailable. Nothing was changed.
